blocks.text: It is a matter of common observation that when external conditions of temperature and pressure are changed, the volume of a given quantity of a gas is affected.

blocks.title: Gas laws
blocks.text: The gas laws describe the relationships between volume of a given amount of gas and the prevailing conditions of temperature and pressure.
While describing Boyle’s and Charles’ laws, some of the variables are held constant during the changes produced in the gases. According to Boyle’s law.

blocks.latex: V \propto \frac{1}{P} \qquad \text{(when } n \text{ and } T \text{ are held constant)} \quad \ldots\ldots\ (1)
V \propto T \qquad \text{(when } n \text{ and } P \text{ are held constant)} \quad \ldots\ldots\ (2)
blocks.text_alt: V ∝ T   (when ‘n’ and ‘P’ are held constant) …… (2)

blocks.text: According to Avogadro’s law volume of the given gas at constant temperature and pressure is directly proportional to the number of moles.

blocks.latex: V \propto n \qquad \text{(when } P \text{ and } T \text{ are held constant)} \quad \ldots\ldots\ (3)
blocks.text_alt: V ∝ n   (when P and T are held constant) …… (3)

The equation (4) is called the ideal gas equation.
